liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Peggy-O** (3 reviews): Jerry wailed through the solo while Keith played sweetly on the pseudo-harpsichord; Keith and Jerry took the tender tune away in a regal performance [9][13][18]
- **Candyman** (1 review): Candyman and Peggy-O are highlighted as worth a good listen [17]
- **Lazy Lightnin'** (1 review): The transition into Supplication and Deal was so energetic it caused head-whiplash [8]
- **Playing In The Band** (1 review): The sandwich of songs including The Other One and Drums is amazing [19]
- **Johnny B. Goode** (1 review): The band clearly enjoyed playing this song, indicated by their enthusiasm [14]

## The recordings

- **gd1977-10-30.sbd.miller.99765.sbeok.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 19 songs; 154 min; rated 4.67/5 by 6 [1]. Said about its sound: The recording has killer sound quality [19]
- **gd1977-10-30.sbd.miller.99838.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 19 songs; 155 min; rated 4.5/5 by 4 [2]
- **gd1977-10-30.137374.mtx.dusborne.flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 19 songs; 157 min; rated 1.25/5 by 4 [3]
- **gd77-10-30.sbd.nawrocki.14946.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 19 songs; 142 min; rated 4.15/5 by 13 [4]
- **gd1977-10-30.sbd.allred.7564.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 19 songs; 147 min; rated 4/5 by 2 [5]. Said about its sound: The recording is tinny but features Godchaux's harpsichord-like tunes floating through the mix; Static from Bobby's guitar occurred during tuning, and he mentioned a ground problem [5][17]

## Around the show

- Jerry told Weir to stop babysitting the guitar and actually play it [10]
- The second set moved well after the band finished their tuning [11]
- Ground fog held the reviewer's flight out of Bloomington, allowing them to stay [14]
- Jerry initially wanted to play Bertha and Fire on the Mountain next [15]
- Phil suggested the Playing In The Band, Wheel, and Wharf Rat sequence [15]
- Similar versions were played two days later and again on December 30, 1977 [9]
- The performance was mellower than the November 4 and 6, 1977 shows [10]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1977-10-30.sbd.miller.99765.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Master Reel -> PCM -> Dat [1]. Also: A tuning track was created for disc changes, and a reel flip was crossfaded [1]
- **gd1977-10-30.sbd.miller.99838.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Master Reel -> PCM -> Dat [2]. Also: Transferred from Sony ECM-990 to master cassette, then reel, then CD [2]
- **gd1977-10-30.137374.mtx.dusborne.flac16**: transferred by Matrix by Dave Usborne; source: 2 Source Matrix by Dusborne; Soundboard (shnid:99838), Recording Info: SBD -> Master Reel -> PCM -> Dat,Transfer Info:Dat -> Samplitude Professional v10.21 ->… [3]. Also: The source is a 1977-10-30 soundboard recording with specific setlist details [3]
- **gd77-10-30.sbd.nawrocki.14946.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [4]. Also: The soundboard captures stage details lost in older low-generation Maxell recordings [13]
- **gd1977-10-30.sbd.allred.7564.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Bob Allred; source: sbd>mr>pcm>dat>cdr>eac [5]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Serigraphics: [Grateful Dead Indiana University Assembly Hall 1977 Concert Poster](https://concertposterauction.com/Listing/Details/1257822/Grateful-Dead-Indiana-University-Assembly-Hall-1977-Concert-Poster) [21]
- Fan art by Serigraphics: [Grateful Dead Indiana University Assembly Hall 1977 Concert Poster](https://concertposterauction.com/Listing/Details/1257822/Grateful-Dead-Indiana-University-Assembly-Hall-1977-Concert-Poster) [22]
- Poster by Antoine Julien There: [Grateful Dead - Indiana Rock History](https://indianarockhistory.com/concert/grateful-dead-3/) [23]
